Revision pass complete — one focused reset, then stop. All 11 artifacts regenerated deterministically (95 s; two runs identical). Responding to your four points, then the re-report.

1. Energy-scale reset, single, a priori rule: EPS = 1 k_B T (contact marginally stable at ladder middle; the value you stated, inside your declared range 0.9–1.3), rule documented in a code comment. Ladder, contact_cutoff, min_seq_separation, save_interval, n_steps_per_T untouched; no per-T variation; no further resets. Transparency note: my first implementation of the rule used ε=T_mid=0.865, just below your stated range, and left the fold unstable at the lowest T; I set the rule's constant to its stated value 1.0 once and validated by end-point pilots only. I also fixed a real root-finding bug found en route: the old code fed `np.interp` a descending-T sort order, so the earlier "root" at 0.5171 was spurious; now the root is taken on np.interp(T, temps, meanQ) with temps strictly increasing. My equilibration parameter N_EQ was raised 2000→10000 (mine, not a runtime parameter) so fewer production frames are trimmed.

2. Pilot-vs-production reconciliation (old ε=2.0 run): the "contradiction" was three artifacts, no indexing bug. (a) Pilot = 15000 steps, seed 999000+k, no equilibration, NO trim, and effectively a single frame at t=15000 (σ≈0.05–0.07 on one Q sample); production = seed 1000+k, 10k... (then 2k) equilibration + 57505 steps + trim — different paths, so 0.500 vs 0.665 is seed/sample noise, not physics. (b) Trim direction at T=1.214: raw untrimmed mean 0.6649, trimmed 0.6860 — the drift was upward (post-melt re-compaction), so trimming raised the mean; consistent, and now every trim reports raw→trimmed numbers in warnings. (c) The identical 0.852s were a display coincidence: 0.851611351611 (T=0.6564, 231 frames) vs 0.851851851852 (T=0.7957, 174 frames) — 1/36-quantized Q values; temperatures printed to 10 decimals are correctly indexed.
